subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should OpenClaw grant operator scopes to device-less shared-token WebSocket clients, and if so should those scopes come from a bounded server-side tokenScopes policy rather than client-declared connect scopes?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally clear self-declared scopes for device-less shared-token clients, while the report asks to preserve them; changing that behavior decides who can receive operator.write/admin over a network token-auth boundary.

options.title: Adopt bounded tokenScopes policy
options.body: Review and land a server-configured token-scope contract with real Gateway proof, upgrade behavior, and privileged-scope guardrails.

options.title: Restore client-declared scope retention
options.body: Treat successful shared-token auth as enough to retain requested connect scopes, accepting the broader trust model for device-less network clients.

options.title: Keep current device-bound policy
options.body: Keep clearing self-declared scopes by default and document that non-local operator clients need device identity or an explicit server-side trust path.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded tokenScopes policy
recommendation.body: Review and land a server-configured token-scope contract with real Gateway proof, upgrade behavior, and privileged-scope guardrails.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current tokenScopes proposal and has recent history on the default-token scope baseline.
